messages:
ravi: Heads-up: landed a docs + SDK change that affects telemetry opt-in behavior in the next SDK minor (redwood-sdk 2.5.0). Default telemetry toggles are being flipped to opt-in for the hosted CLI.
claire: summary of what changed and why?
ravi: TL;DR: telemetry collection (anonymous usage pings and optional error traces) remains off for the SDK core, but the CLI previously defaulted to opt-out (enabled). We're changing the CLI default to opt-in = false and adding a clear 'telemetry enable' workflow in the CLI and docs. This aligns with our privacy policy and customer feedback.
paul: does this affect customers on Dedicated or Private?
ravi: No change to Dedicated/Private control planes. Those deployments already require explicit admin consent during install. This change only affects the open-source CLI distributed with hosted SDK packages.
docs-bot: Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1133 "CLI telemetry: opt-in default, enable workflow, and migration guidance". Includes examples, FAQ, and release note blurb.
paul: is there a migration path for teams that relied on telemetry for early-alerting?
ravi: Yes  we added: 1) a compatibility flag `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LEGACY=1` available for 45 days, 2) a migration snippet to enable a consent flow in CI/deploy pipelines, and 3) a small server-side webhook to receive telemetry only after explicit consent. Docs include code samples for consent collection.
privacy: Reviewed the language. Added required disclosure text for onboarding screens and a short paragraph for customer-facing release notes.
release-bot: Release note draft: "Behavioral change: The CLI now defaults telemetry to disabled. To preserve existing telemetry, set REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LEGACY=1 or run `redwood-cli telemetry enable --consent-file path/to/consent.json`"
claire: can you paste the CI/consent snippet?
ravi: sure:```bash
# CI: do not enable telemetry by default, collect consent explicitly
if [ -f /workspace/telemetry_consent.json ]; then
  redwood-cli telemetry enable --consent-file /workspace/telemetry_consent.json || true
else
  echo "No telemetry consent found; telemetry remains disabled"
fi
# legacy compatibility (temporary)
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LEGACY=${REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LEGACY:-0}
if [ "$REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LEGACY" = "1" ]; then
  echo "Legacy telemetry enabled by env flag"
fi
```
paul: what's the deprecation timeline for the legacy env flag?
ravi: Legacy flag will be supported for 45 days after the stable 2.5.0 release. We'll post reminders at 30 and 10 days. After 45 days the flag will be removed and teams must use explicit enable workflows.
docs-bot: Changelog entry added: "telemetry: CLI default changed to disabled; compatibility flag available for 45 days; migration guide included". Risk: low.
claire: any analytics/monitoring considerations for internal teams that relied on the data?
ravi: Yes  we captured a historical snapshot export for internal analytics teams. We'll retain a rolling 30-day export before cutover. If teams need extended history, file a request with analytics.
privacy: added wording for customer emails and support templates. Also added a short FAQ: "Why the change? privacy-first defaults; no product telemetry loss for Dedicated/Private; opt-in recommended for hosted non-sensitive telemetry."
paul: i'll coordinate a brief announcement in #eng and notify platform consumers. Also flag support so they can update customer templates.
claire: thanks. small ask: add a one-line to the CLI help output explaining default and the compatibility flag.
ravi: done in PR. Also added `redwood-cli telemetry status` to inspect current state.
release-bot: Docs site build succeeded: https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/telemetry.
paul: ok, i'll schedule the customer-facing note for the release day and ping the security/privacy reviewers. Thanks everyone."
